identify.intro: Ex-army trucks have been repowered, re-cabbed and converted, and several 435 variants look almost the same. Use the type number, the engine plate and the axles to work out what you're looking at.

items.head: Type number in the chassis number
items.body: The chassis number starts with the type: 435.115 is the U 1300 L, 435.117 the U 1300 L/37, 435.110 the U 1700, 435.111 the U 1700 L and 435.113 the U 1700 L/38. Early trucks read like 43511510…; later ones carry a 17-digit WDB4351151W… VIN.

items.head: Cab number plate
items.body: The 435 uses the 425-series cab, which carries a body-number plate reading 425.820. The 435 always has a full cab; a convertible cab points to a different series, such as the Turkish-built 436.

items.head: Engine
items.body: The naturally aspirated 5.7 OM 352 (catalogued as OM 353.959/.961) was standard. The turbo OM 352A and the 6.0 OM 366/366A followed, the OM 366 from 1987. Turbo engines take different injector nozzles, and naturally aspirated U1300Ls take their own water pump.

items.head: 6-lug vs 10-lug axles
items.body: U 1300 Ls run 6-lug disc-brake axles with M18 x 1.5 studs. U 1700 types use 10-lug axles, which owners say don't have the 6-lug trucks' front breather pumping problem.

items.head: Military spec
items.body: Bundeswehr and US Army Europe trucks are 24-volt and basically trimmed, and some have no hydraulic system. Military contract plates let you trace a truck's service history.

values.intro: Plain ex-army U1300Ls have come down from their 2023 peak, while finished campers and refurbished crew cabs still bring big money.
values.note: Based on 12 Bring a Trailer U1300L sales from 2019 to October 2026. Utility and ex-army trucks sold for $25,000–47,305. One 1987 utility truck went from $45,000 in March 2025 to $43,000 in June 2026 and $29,500 in October 2026. Refurbished stock trucks sold for $54,500–72,900 in 2022–23. Camper conversions brought $102,000 and $175,111, and a refurbished 1980 DoKa sold for $95,000 in March 2026.

paragraphs: Nearly every 435 in the US is a used import, usually ex-Bundeswehr. Military trucks reach the market through German federal surplus sales (VEBEG) and European dealers. One Steel Soldiers member found trucks at VEBEG for around €12,000–15,000, but warned about language, inspection, shipping of $5,000 or more, and customs. RoRo shipping is priced by volume, and a container may mean taking the wheels off.

The 435 was built until 1993, so every one is now past NHTSA's 25-year exemption. In older threads, owners noted that not all U1300Ls were DOT-exempt when younger, and that exemption usually depended on age or a camper conversion. US-titled trucks on Bring a Trailer have carried clean titles from Montana, Washington and Mississippi, but registration of a 7.5-tonne air-braked truck varies by state. Ask your DMV before you buy.

Members of the same thread said US prices for nice trucks ran about $25,000–60,000, and that after fees and paperwork, buying in Europe can cost about the same as buying domestically, with more hassle. Recent BaT results bear that out at the lower end.

production.intro: Gaggenau built 30,726 trucks in the 435 series in eight variants from 1975 to 1993. The U 1300 L made up most of them (Wikipedia, Mercedes-Benz).
